claims.text: The uncoated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response.
The uncoated alloy has poor mechanical integrity and cracks under applied-field or pressure-field operation.
Bulk (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 samples can be synthesized by standard melting routes.
A conformal sub-micron to few-micron copper coating can be deposited on the alloy by PVD.
The deposited copper film will be continuous and well adhered.
The metallic film will bridge surface flaws and act as a crack-arrest layer at the alloy–coating interface.
Copper has sufficient ductility and toughness to blunt crack tips during field-induced deformation.
The copper coating will redistribute local stresses during field-induced deformation.
Crack-tip blunting and stress redistribution will raise the effective compressive strength and inhibit catastrophic fracture.
A thin, conformal copper coating will minimally dilute or perturb the intrinsic caloric phase transformation of the underlying alloy.
Copper-coated samples will have greater compressive strength than uncoated samples.
Copper-coated samples will exhibit reduced crack propagation and improved damage tolerance relative to uncoated samples.
The field- and pressure-induced caloric response of coated samples will remain essentially unchanged relative to the uncoated alloy.
The coating will remain effective near ambient to moderately elevated temperatures, under the original applied-field and pressure conditions, and during quasi-static compression.
An overly thick copper coating might dampen the functional caloric effect.
A poorly bonded coating might introduce a thermal barrier.
